text:
incident-bot: URGENT: KV cache growth detected on prod-serving-1 (spec-decode path). Error rate rising >3x for /v1/chat and /v1/generate. Paging SRE oncall @sre-oncall :rotating_light:

eli: seeing large mem delta on kvcache shards, continuous-batcher queues spiking. graphs: https://grafana.internal/r/abc123 (highly red)

maya: confirmed elevated tail latency and ~10% 5xx on chat for the last 6m. a few customers reported timeouts.

anika: initial suspicion: speculative decoding generating many divergent drafts that miss KV prefix reuse. each draft creates extra KV entries, plus continuous batching keeps them hot -> cache blowup.

jordan: can we toggle speculative off quickly per pool?

sre-oncall: i'm on it. handoff notes: grabbing logs, will try isolated toggle on canary nodes first. @opsbot run top-pods --label serving=prod-serving-1

opsbot: output:
```
POD                          CPU%   MEM%   KV_CACHE_MB
serving-1-0                  12%    78%    12500
serving-1-1                  15%    81%    12840
serving-1-2 (canary)         11%    42%    4200
```

eli: can we reduce batch window and disable speculative on the canary then watch tail latency?

anika: yes. quick mitigations recommended:
- speculative_decoding.enabled = false (per-pool)
- continuous_batch.max_window_tokens = 512 -> 256
- kv_cache.draft_prefix_ttl = 30s (temporarily)

eli: applying patch to canary config now. command:
```
curl -X PATCH https://config.internal/api/v1/pools/prod-serving-1 \  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \  -d '{"speculative_decoding": {"enabled": false}, "continuous_batch": {"max_window_tokens": 256}, "kv_cache": {"draft_prefix_ttl_s": 30}}'
```

opsbot: canary patch applied to serving-1-2. monitoring for 2 minutes

maya: within 90s I see request queue length drop on canary and 5xxs fall to baseline there.

cs-lucy: Customer impact: three mid-market customers reported intermittent timeouts for chat/embeddings during the spike. One CS escalated to enterprise contact. No data exfiltration. They are being notified with 'service degradation' note.

eli: rolling change to remainder of pool with incremental 10% steps and health checks. plan to keep speculative disabled until further postmortem.

jordan: we should also enable a short-lived eviction policy for draft prefixes to prevent long tail accumulation. logging added to track eviction rate.

anika: added an alert for "kv_cache.prefetch_count" and "spec_decoding.draft_divergence_ratio" to catch this earlier.

opsbot: rollout summary: patched 1/3 canary -> ok, 2/3 next -> ok, 3/3 -> patched. memory usage trending down.

maya: metrics now: error rate back within SLO, p95 latency improved to pre-incident numbers.

sre-oncall: incident mitigated. immediate customer impact contained. Escalation: none further.

sam: taking night oncall handoff. key things for night:
- watch kv_cache.size_by_prefix (alert threshold lowered)
- monitor draft_divergence_ratio and continuous_batch.queue_len
- rollback plan: if errors increase, revert batch window to 512 and re-enable speculative for fairness, then ring SRE lead
- runbook link: https://wiki.internal/runbooks/kvcache-spec-decode

sre-oncall: assigning postmortem to @anika. immediate action items:
- (P1) Add automated kill-switch for speculative per-pool (owner: eng-runtime)
- (P2) Add pre-deploy simulation to flag high draft divergence on canary (owner: eng-ml)
- (P3) Revisit default continuous_batch window heuristics (owner: eng-platform)

anika: noted. will draft postmortem and include timeline, dump of top keys, and suggested long-term fixes (kv sharding heuristics, better draft deduping).

elI: small follow-up: please capture a sample of top 100 draft prefixes and their TTLs, attach to PM.

cs-lucy: customer comms: sent 'we experienced degraded availability; mitigations applied; investigating root cause; will follow up with postmortem' to affected accounts.

sre-oncall: closing thread for active mitigation. reopening if anything regresses. Thanks all for fast response :thumbsup:
